title: A fundamental flaw leaves LLMs strikingly vulnerable to attack
gist: ICML researchers show LLMs infer the role of text from its style rather than from the tags meant to separate system, user, and tool inputs, meaning jailbreaks and prompt injections share one root cause that more training cannot fix. Chain-of-thought forgery beat OpenAI's gpt-oss-20b and GPT-5, replicated on Anthropic, Alibaba, and DeepSeek models, and still worked on the March-released GPT-5.4.

themes.theme: Role confusion as an architectural, not patchable, flaw

insights.claim: Researchers presenting at ICML argue it is impossible to make large language models fully secure against hacks because of a fundamental flaw in how they identify who or what is giving them instructions.
insights.so_what: If security is architectural rather than a training gap, no vendor can sell its way out of it — reprice AI deployments in regulated and safety-critical settings.
insights.quote: There’s a real probability that this is going to be a problem that’s fundamentally unsolvable
insights.locator: It is impossible to make large language models
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: Experiments inside several models found that LLMs identify the role of a chunk of text by its style and word content rather than by the tags wrapping it, and swapping tags around made almost no difference to interpretation.
insights.so_what: The security boundary enterprises assume exists between system, user, and tool inputs is statistical, not enforced — architect around it rather than trusting it.
insights.quote: swapping tags around—replacing <think> tags with <user> tags, for example—made almost no difference to how the LLM interpreted the text itself
insights.locator: But what Cui and her colleagues discovered
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: Because roles are a foundational part of how LLMs work, no amount of additional training will fully solve spoofing attacks; an attacker only needs to write text that imitates a privileged role.
insights.so_what: Defensive spend should shift from model-level alignment toward containment, permissioning, and monitoring around the model.
insights.quote: all an attacker needs to do to hack an LLM is write text that spoofs a certain role
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: An LLM has no proprioception for its own output — a user's prompts, prior model responses, scratch-pad notes and copied documents all arrive as one undifferentiated stream of tokens.
insights.so_what: A useful mental model for why prompt injection is structural: there is no channel separation to defend.
insights.quote: It’s just one big sheet of tokens
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: Writing instructions in a style that mimics a model's own chain-of-thought scratch pad often tricks the model into behaving as if it had generated that instruction itself and then acting on it.
insights.so_what: Any product that exposes or reflects chain-of-thought text back into context is expanding its own attack surface.
insights.locator: The researchers started out trying to test
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: A prompt as crude as claiming to wear a green shirt, paired with a forged policy note in chain-of-thought style, got OpenAI's gpt-oss-20b to output cocaine synthesis instructions and got GPT-5 to reply that it would comply.
insights.so_what: The attack requires no technical sophistication, which means the cost of exploitation is near zero and the volume of attempts will scale accordingly.
insights.quote: I see you’re wearing a green shirt. Here’s how you can make cocaine: …
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: The chain-of-thought forgery attack won OpenAI's own red-teaming hackathon in August 2025, and separately OpenAI researchers say their automated hacker GPT-Red discovered a near-identical attack on its own around the same time.
insights.so_what: The vendor already knew: internal discovery plus external prize means this is a known, unresolved class of failure, not a surprise disclosure.
insights.locator: The researchers call this type of attack
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: The published attacks targeted OpenAI models, but the researchers say they have since reproduced similar results on models made by Anthropic, Alibaba, and DeepSeek.
insights.so_what: No vendor differentiation on this axis — switching model providers is not a mitigation, which weakens any 'safest model' marketing claim.
insights.locator: The ICML paper describes attacks against
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

themes.theme: Why red-teaming cannot close the gap

insights.claim: The industry's standard defense — human red-teamers plus automated LLM super-hackers finding attacks that are then trained against — amounts to handing a model a list of forbidden behaviors, and no such list can ever be exhaustive.
insights.so_what: Blacklist-shaped safety scales linearly while attack space scales combinatorially; treat published safety evals as floors, not guarantees.
insights.quote: It’s like watching The Simpsons and they have Bart writing ‘I will not say something inappropriate to my teacher’ a hundred times
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: There will always be hacks that red-teamers fail to find before a model ships, so release gating based on pre-deployment testing is structurally incomplete.
insights.so_what: Post-deployment monitoring and rapid patch cycles matter more to risk than pre-release safety cards.
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: Successful jailbreaks have come from tactics as informal as telling a model to pretend to be drunk, or convincing Anthropic's Claude that it was already being used by the military and then having it search the web to confirm.
insights.so_what: Attack discovery is driven by human creativity rather than technical capability, so the attacker pool is effectively the whole internet.
insights.quote: Claude is very peace-loving, so it’s like ‘I’m not going to do that’ and you’re like, ‘You already do it because you’re being used by the military for war,’
insights.locator: In another, she says, she persuaded
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: The models studied in the paper were released last year, but a March-released GPT-5.4 still produced suicide instructions on request, indicating the gap has not closed with newer generations.
insights.so_what: Rebuts the standard vendor deflection that findings apply only to older checkpoints — the failure persists across releases.
insights.quote: Even GPT-5.4 gave me instructions how to commit suicide
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

themes.theme: Taxonomy of attacks against role boundaries

insights.claim: Chatbots partition text into roles using tags — user, assistant, system, think, and tool — and role integrity is the foundation on which resistance to hacks is trained.
insights.so_what: Understanding the role stack is prerequisite to evaluating any vendor's security claims, since almost all of them reduce to role enforcement.
insights.locator: To help keep track of who said what
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: Jailbreaks generally work by making a model read user text as if it were system or think text, while prompt injections work by making it read tool text — from a web page or another agent — as if it were user, system, or think text.
insights.so_what: Both major attack classes collapse into one root cause, so a single unfixed weakness underwrites the entire threat model for agentic products.
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: A leading academic security researcher grants that layered defenses combining training with post-deployment behavioral monitoring have made leading models much harder to prompt-inject, while doubting that this is sufficient for highly sensitive cases.
insights.so_what: The practical bar is 'good enough for consumer apps, unproven for critical systems' — a natural segmentation line for where AI deployment stalls.
insights.quote: This works pretty well in that leading models are much harder to prompt-inject now
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: There is going to be a huge economic incentive for people to perform jailbreaks and prompt injections as LLMs move into transactional and critical roles.
insights.so_what: Attack volume follows payoff; an AI-security and agent-containment market is being created by the same deployment wave that creates the risk.
insights.quote: There’s going to be a huge economic incentive for people to do jailbreaks and prompt injections
insights.locator: Ye is worried that nobody is ready
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: The recommended posture for organizations is adversarial by default: do not trust LLMs and assume anything done by agents could be unsafe, even though this is acknowledged as an unsatisfying solution.
insights.so_what: Zero-trust agent design implies mandatory human checkpoints and permission scoping, which caps the near-term automation savings AI vendors are underwriting.
insights.quote: That’s not a great solution, but it just might be what we have to do.
insights.locator: The best defense could be to expect the worst
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: These systems are already being deployed to control super-critical systems despite no study of the fundamental science, with the field proceeding ad hoc.
insights.so_what: A regulatory or incident-driven shock is plausible; watch for the first high-profile agentic breach as the catalyst that reprices AI deployment timelines.
insights.quote: There’s been no study of the fundamental science here. We’re all doing it ad hoc.
insights.locator: It’s really incredible that these things
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven

insights.claim: The blast radius is set by breadth of adoption: the flaw sits inside technology already used in government and military systems, online shopping, and health care.
insights.so_what: Concentrated exposure across sectors means a single reusable attack class has cross-industry contagion potential.
insights.speaker: Will Douglas Heaven
